english_retrieval.title: SC sets aside Bombay HC verdict cancelling Amravati MP Navneet Kaur Rana’s caste certificate - The Hindu
english_retrieval.snippet: News and reviews from the world of cinema and streaming. ## Allowing the plea of Ms. Rana, a Bench comprising Justices J.K. Maheshwari and Sanjay Karol said the High Court should not have interfered with the report of the scrutiny committee on the issue of caste certificate of Ms. Rana. The Supreme Court on April 4, 2024, confirmed the validity of the ‘Mochi’ caste certificate of Lok Sabha member Navneet Kaur Rana. “The application (for caste certificate) was made intentionally to make a fraudulent claim to enable Ms. Rana to contest the election for the post of Member of Parliament on a seat reserved for a scheduled castes candidate,” the High Court had concluded. The High Court had passed the order on a plea seeking cancellation of the caste certificate issued by the Mumbai Deputy Collector’s office on August 30, 2013 identifying her as a member of the ‘Mochi’ community. The complaint had alleged that Ms. Rana had obtained the certificate with the influence of her husband, Ravi Rana, who was a member of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly.

A special court granted her bail in that case Wednesday, but Kaur is yet to get a hearing from the Supreme Court in another case, in which she appealed against the Bombay High Court’s cancellation of her Scheduled Caste certificate last year. Navneet Kaur Rana was able to contest the 2019 Lok Sabha elections from Amravati, a reserved seat, because she had a certificate that declared her as belonging to the Mochi (cobbler) Scheduled Caste community.
